game actions have a getItemElements() function you can use to get the elements for the action, so if you wanted to see if your skill contained 3 specific elements it becomes something like
Code:
[1,2,3].every(e => action.getItemElements().includes(e))
where the array is the list of elements youre checking

this.result().isHit() works specifically in notetags where the "this" refers to the action being done. youll have to change the "this" to "target" within the action sequence for the same effect.
do keep in mind, this only check if the most recent hit didnt miss. if a skill hits multiple times, then the code will only check if the hit immediately before the check missed or not

reifferm said:
I'm questioning myself if is really needed to use nested condition for that, or i can just add a one more && with the condition i wish to check
Click to expand...
you never *needed* the nested conditions for this, but nesting multiple IFs is logically equivalent to using multiple &&s. if you only want one damage type to trigger the thing you want, then it can be done in one IF. if you want a different animation for the "damage types" youll want to do some nesting since the 3rd condition has different outcomes.

then the function you use is isWtypeEquipprd(x) where x is the id of the weapon type, but as enemies dont have equipment, they dont have that function and itll cause an error when an enemy uses it.
Youd have to either give enemies a version of the attack without that function or use isActor() at the start to make sure it doesnt get ran on an a enemy.
